_readme: Ratchet baselines for tier-B gates (see tools/run_all_gates.py).
A tier-B gate tracks debt that cannot be paid down yet, so it is allowed to fail;
what it may NOT do is move silently. actual == total and the per-code detail must
match exactly, otherwise the run fails in one of three directions:
DRIFT+  debt grew    -> someone introduced new defects
DRIFT-  debt shrank  -> an improvement was absorbed; lower 'total' BY HAND and
write down why, or the number stops tracking anything
DRIFT~  same total, different mix -> one defect kind was traded for another
This file is edited by hand on purpose. There is no --write-baseline flag: an
auto-update would let any regression be absorbed by re-running the harness once,
which is precisely the fake gate this project keeps running into.
Values must come from a real run, never from an estimate.
A 'total: 0' entry is NOT usable: with no findings the parsed composition is {},
which can never equal the recorded detail ({T1: 0}), so it would report DRIFT~.
Record the real nonzero codes even when they are few.
